content: 1. Atropine and eluxadoline may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. Co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation should also be avoided, as this increases the risk of serious constipation-related adverse reactions. 2. Glucagon can increase the effects of atropine through mechanisms involving additive inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. Co-administration of anticholinergic drugs and glucagon should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as this combination increases the risk of gastrointestinal adverse reactions. 3. Intranasal glucagon also increases the effects of atropine through similar mechanisms. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs due to the risk of additive gastrointestinal motility inhibition. 4. Glycopyrronium tosylate (topical) and atropine may enhance each other's effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as this combination may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 5. Atropine and macimorelin may interact through an unspecified mechanism. Drugs that blunt the growth hormone (GH) response to macimorelin may affect the accuracy of diagnostic tests. Sufficient washout time of drugs affecting GH release should be allowed before administering macimorelin. 6. Pramlintide and atropine may synergistically inhibit gastrointestinal motility. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 7. Revefenacin and atropine both reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Co-administration may lead to additive anticholinergic effects, so alternative drugs should be considered or therapy should be closely monitored. 8. Atropine decreases the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Concomitant use of anticholinergic drugs may cause a hyporesponse to stimulation testing with secretin. Anticholinergic drugs should be discontinued at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 9. Sofpironium topical and atropine may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 10. Co-administration with other anticholinergic-containing drugs should be avoided due to the risk of additive anticholinergic adverse effects. 11. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 12.
